questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code acquires locks for a transfer? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Three adjust() calls for the same bin and SKU start at the same time. How does KeyedMutex order them?
choices: They run one at a time, in the order acquire() was called, because each caller waits on the previous tail promise
They run concurrently because the JavaScript event loop is single-threaded and no lock is needed
They run one at a time but in arbitrary order, depending on which repository call resolves first
Only the first runs; the other two are rejected because the key is already present in the map

questions.prompt: move() throws InsufficientStockError while transfer() holds both locks. What happens to the locks?
choices: Both stay held until the process restarts
The destination lock is released but the source lock stays held
Both are released by the nested finally blocks, inner lock first
Neither is released, but the next acquire() for those keys times out and clears them

questions.prompt: Why does adjust() re-read the stock inside the lock instead of accepting a quantity read by the caller beforehand?
choices: Reading inside the lock is faster because the repository caches locked keys
A value read before locking may be stale by the time the write happens, causing lost updates
The repository throws if get() is called without holding a lock
It avoids allocating a new BinStock object for missing rows
